name: Swann 2002: six counter-clockwise configurations as printed (exact Thomas)
origin: Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook (Laurentian University), the lab's standard circumcerebral protocol (Cook et al. 1999), given once to Ingo Swann in August 1998
summary: The 30-min exposure Persinger's lab gave the artist and remote viewer Ingo Swann: three burst-firing and three frequency-modulated (Thomas) configurations of 5 min each, rotated counter-clockwise around the head with the point durations, gaps and per-coil timing printed in the paper's Table 1. The lab reported altered experiences during the fields; one subject.
notes: Table 1, read from the page scan: pixel (point) duration 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 3 ms; interstimulus time 1, 1, 3000, 1, 1, 3000 ms; commutator rate 20, 100, 200 ms and change in rate +2, +20, -2, for B1-B3 and again for T1-T3. Commutator rate is read as the time on the first coil and change in rate as the change at each following coil, as the lab later defined "20+2"; that reading is an interpretation. The signs are read literally: each next coil gets 2 ms more in the +2 rows (20 to 34 ms), 20 ms more in the +20 rows (100 to 240 ms) and 2 ms less in the -2 rows (200 to 186 ms). Persinger & Lavallee 2010 use "+" to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms and 200 to 214 ms; the literal reading was chosen because the +20 rows cannot shorten seven times from 100 ms, Cook 1999's full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms fit it better (216 ms per turn at 20 to 34 ms, 104 ms at 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published. The paper puts eight equally spaced solenoids in the plane "between the midforehead and above the ears"; the ring here is Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2 on the 10% line, coil 1 left frontal and coil 8 right prefrontal as the lab later described its ring (Persinger & Lavallee 2010), an inference. The Thomas (frequency-modulated) pulse plays from its exact 849-point table; the burst-firing point values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst stands in (230 points, 6 -> 30 Hz at 3 ms per point and three times faster at 1 ms). Intensity 2-5 uT in the paper; 3.5 uT is the midpoint. Differences from military-p06-persinger-swann-1998: that preset gives B2/T2 3-ms and B3/T3 1-ms points (the scan shows 1, 1, 3), a synthetic Thomas sweep and an Fpz-Oz ring. During the Thomas patterns Swann reported floating in and out of his body (T1), pressure in his ear and a marked suppression of his remote-viewing images (T2), and seeing the three experimenters as skeletons (T3). On later days, 7-Hz spike-and-slow-wave activity over his occipital lobes correlated (rho = .50) with blind accuracy ratings; the paper does not test whether the fields changed accuracy. One subject, no sham, unblinded exposure, and a follow-up pilot (Koren & Persinger 2002) reported that accuracy fell when weak Windows-generated, but not DOS-generated, fields were run around the targets, which shows how loosely controlled the setup was. For a self-test, randomise blinded active and sham sessions and have remote-viewing trials judged blind. No independent replication. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Blindfolded in a comfortable chair in a quiet, dark room; speak your impressions aloud and record them (Swann wore a lapel microphone in an acoustic chamber). Remote-viewing trials followed on later days: hidden pictures or objects in envelopes about 6 m away, 2-3 min of drawing each.
schedule: One exposure in the original, followed by remote-viewing trials on the next days.
source: Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, Remote viewing with the artist Ingo Swann, Percept Mot Skills 94:927-949 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ (full-text scan with Table 1 https://www.remoteviewed.com/biblo/papers/INGO%20SWANN%20NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL%20PROFILE-ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHIC%20CORRELATES-MAGNETIC%20RESONANCE%20IMAGING%20AND%20POSSIBLE%20MECHANISMS.pdf) ; Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61-64 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (the "20+2" notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal; sibling study retold) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Lehman 2016, MSc thesis, Laurentian University, pp. 56-57 ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms; counter-clockwise standard) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 (230-point increasing-frequency pattern at 1 ms) https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Koren & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 95:989-998 (fields around the target, pilot) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12509207/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/

B3 burst 3 ms pts, 3 s gap, 200->186 ms/coil (200-2)
T1 Thomas 1 ms pts, 1 ms gap, 20->34 ms/coil (20+2)
T2 Thomas 1 ms pts, 1 ms gap, 100->240 ms/coil (100+20)
